# Simple Shot Timer

> Simple Shot Timer is the free and open-source shot timer app, with no ads and no data tracking. It is available on Android and iPhone (iOS). It turns a phone into a shot timer for dry-fire and live-fire practice: a par timer that also hears your shots. It detects shots through the microphone, shows splits live, runs Standard, Par and Stage drills, saves the drills you run often and keeps every string on the phone.

Website: https://simpleshottimer.com/

## At a glance

- The free and open-source shot timer app (GPL-3.0-only). No ads, no data tracking.
- Price: $0. No ads, subscriptions or in-app purchases. A dedicated shot timer costs $100 or more.
- 3 drill modes: Standard, Par and Stage.
- Stages of up to 200 seconds.
- Up to 5,000 strings kept in the history (the cap is adjustable from 50 to 5,000; default 500).
- 8 languages: English, Deutsch, Español, Suomi, Français, Polski, Português, Русский.
- Platforms: Android and iPhone (iOS).
- Open source under GPL-3.0-only, with additional attribution terms under section 7 (NOTICE file in the repository).

## How it works

### Start: Stand by. Beep. Go.

Choose an instant, fixed or random start delay. The screen shows STAND BY, like a range officer after "make ready", then the beep. The clock starts when the beep is heard, not when the phone asks for it: the app measures the beep through the microphone, so speaker lag never ends up in your time. The beep is a 2,325 Hz tone, the pitch range used by most club shot timers; the start beep is short and the par beep is longer.

### Detection: Hears every shot.

Shots are picked up from the raw microphone signal with the phone's voice processing switched off. A notch at the beep's pitch keeps the beep out, an echo filter ignores reflections off walls and baffles, and a shot fired during the beep still counts.

### Results: Every split, the second you stop.

Total time, first shot and last split are on screen the moment you press STOP. The review lists every shot with its split, adds fastest, slowest and average, and takes a label, notes and a penalty. Shots can be added or deleted by hand in the review.

### Drills: Standard, Par or Stage.

Run an open string (Standard), use it as a par timer with repeat cycles and a rest between them (Par), or time a whole IPSC, USPSA or IDPA stage of up to 200 seconds (Stage). Shots are detected in every mode, so Par mode also shows the splits of every cycle. Save the drills you run often under a name and load any of them with one tap from the Drills tab; each saved drill can be renamed, overwritten or deleted.

### History: Every string, kept.

Each run is saved on your phone together with the drill it was shot with. Keep up to 5,000 strings, look back any time and export one string or your whole history as CSV through the share sheet. A run that detects no shots is not saved unless you add a shot by hand.

## Details

- Auto-configure: fire a few shots with your usual gun and stance, and the app suggests a sensitivity and frequency band tuned to what it heard on that range. Both can also be set by hand.
- Live mic test: a level meter with the threshold line, to dial in sensitivity before going hot.
- Flash and buzz on the beep: each beep comes with a screen flash and a haptic, timed to land with the sound. Turn the beep volume to 0 to train silently on the flash. With the system's reduced-motion setting on, a gentle edge ring replaces the flash.
- Keeps running in the background: switch apps or lock the screen mid-string; detection and par beeps carry on.
- Honest times on any speaker: for a Bluetooth speaker or earbuds the mic can't hear, a manual latency offset keeps the clock starting on the sound.
- Never miss a beep: if the media volume is muted while a string runs, a one-line notice says so. On Android, tapping it opens the volume panel.
- Themes: follow the system, or pick light, dark or high contrast, all in the app's black-and-white look.
- Keep the screen awake during a string; optional haptic on every beep.
- Navigation: four tabs (Timer, Drills, History, Settings). The tab bar is inert while a string is running.

## Privacy

Your strings stay on your phone.

- No account: there is nothing to sign up for.
- No ads, no tracking: no analytics, advertising or tracking code. The app sends nothing off your phone.
- Nothing recorded: the mic signal is analysed in memory while the app listens (during a string, the mic test or auto-configure). Audio is never saved or sent. The app needs microphone permission to time a string.
- Data the app stores (strings, shot times, settings) lives in a local SQLite database and preferences file on the device. It can be viewed, edited, exported as CSV and deleted in the app; uninstalling removes everything.
- The website simpleshottimer.com sets no cookies, loads nothing from third parties and has no analytics. It is hosted by Netlify, which processes access data (such as IP address and time of request) to deliver the pages; server logs are deleted after 30 days at the latest.
- App privacy policy: https://simpleshottimer.com/privacy/
- Website privacy policy: https://simpleshottimer.com/privacy/website/

## FAQ

### Is there a free shot timer app?

Yes, Simple Shot Timer is free on iPhone and Android, with no ads, no subscriptions and no in-app purchases. It's open source under GPLv3, and there is no account to create.

### Can I use my phone as a shot timer?

Yes. With a shot timer app, your phone gives the start beep, hears your shots through the microphone and shows every split. Tune the detection once for each range, keep the mic uncovered, and turn on the screen flash if the beep is hard to hear through ear protection. How to use your phone as a shot timer (https://simpleshottimer.com/guides/phone-shot-timer/) walks you through it.

### Will it replace a real shot timer?

Not completely. The app is limited by your phone's hardware, so it can't reach the level of a decent dedicated timer. It's a solid alternative if you don't want to spend $100 or more on a range timer, or if you left yours at home. Shot timer app or dedicated shot timer? (https://simpleshottimer.com/guides/shot-timer-app-vs-dedicated-timer/) compares the two honestly.

### What's the difference between a par timer and a shot timer?

A par timer only beeps: a start beep, and a par beep when your time is up. A shot timer also listens for your shots and times every split. Simple Shot Timer does both, so you can train against a par and still see your splits. Par timer vs. shot timer (https://simpleshottimer.com/guides/par-timer-vs-shot-timer/) explains when each one is enough.

### Does it work for live fire?

Yes. Fire a few shots with Auto-configure and the app suggests a sensitivity and frequency band for that gun and range. On a busy line, a shot from the next bay can register if it is as loud as yours; you can delete it in the review.

### Can I use it for dry fire?

Yes. Par mode gives you a start beep and a par beep to beat, with repeat cycles and a rest between them, so it also works as an interval timer for dry-fire reps. A dry-fire click is quiet, so either raise the sensitivity until it registers or simply shoot against the par time.

### Will a Bluetooth speaker throw off my times?

No. The clock starts when the mic hears the beep, so the speaker's lag is measured, not guessed. For sound the mic can't hear, such as earbuds, set a manual latency offset in Settings.

### Is there an iPhone version?

Yes. It's free on the App Store for iPhone (https://apps.apple.com/app/simple-shot-timer/id6819042653), just as it is on Google Play for Android.

### Does the app record me?

No. While the app listens (during a string, the mic test or auto-configure), the mic signal is analysed in memory and is never saved or sent. Your strings and settings are stored only on your phone.

### Can I get my data out?

Yes. Export a single string or your whole history as CSV through the share sheet and open it in any spreadsheet, to track your progress or to share with your firearms instructor.

## Guides

- How to use your phone as a shot timer: microphone permission, Auto-configure and the mic test, the frequency band filter, where to put the phone, hearing the beep through ear protection (screen flash, vibration), Bluetooth speakers and the latency offset for earbuds, busy ranges, saved drills, history and CSV. https://simpleshottimer.com/guides/phone-shot-timer/
- Dry-fire par drills with par times: dry-fire safety rules, how par time training works and how to pick a par, and five classic drills (draw to first shot, ready to first shot, reload, target transitions, strong hand and weak hand only) with starting par times and Par mode settings. https://simpleshottimer.com/guides/dry-fire-par-drills/
- Shot timer app or dedicated shot timer?: an honest comparison of beep loudness, microphone and fast splits, neighbouring bays, battery, price and history, when a dedicated timer is worth buying, and which one to buy (CED7000 GEN-2, PACT Club Timer III, Competition Electronics ProTimer and ProTimer BT, AMG Lab Commander, Shooters Global SG Timer GO and SG Timer 2). https://simpleshottimer.com/guides/shot-timer-app-vs-dedicated-timer/
- Par timer vs. shot timer: what's the difference?: a par timer gives a start beep and a par beep and doesn't listen; a shot timer hears your shots and records every split. A par timer is enough for dry fire; on the range, shot detection shows where the time went. Simple Shot Timer does both. https://simpleshottimer.com/guides/par-timer-vs-shot-timer/
- Free shot timer apps compared: eight free and freemium shot timer and par timer apps for iPhone and Android (Simple Shot Timer, ShootOnTime: Par Timer, Par Timer Pro, IPSC Shot Timer, PlinkPal, Shot Timer – Range Trainer, Range Buddy, Shot Timer – Measure & Improve), compared on whether they hear your shots, platforms, price, Google Play's ads label and the stores' privacy labels, from the store listings on 22 October 2026. https://simpleshottimer.com/guides/free-shot-timer-apps/

All guides are also in German: https://simpleshottimer.com/de/ratgeber/
